desktopOnly: Open Shroudly from the desktop app to use this.
statsInactiveHint: Start protection to see live traffic.
onlineNowDesc: People using Shroudly right now, worldwide
glassSurfaceDesc: Frosted, translucent panels over a tinted glow in your accent colour. Text keeps its own colours, so nothing becomes harder to read.
stratSplitMid: Split in the middle of SNI
autoModeDesc: Find a working strategy for each blocked site automatically
dnsProtectionDesc: Resolve names over encrypted DNS (DoH) so blocks and forged replies are bypassed
preferIpv6Desc: Use IPv6 for outgoing connections when available
startOnBootDesc: Launch Shroudly automatically when you sign in to your computer
minimizeToTrayDesc: Keep running in the system tray when the window is closed
showNotificationsDesc: Show a system notification when protection starts or stops
shareOnlineCount: Count me in the live total
shareOnlineCountDesc: Sends a random number that changes every launch, so the app can show how many copies are running. It is only sent while protection is on, so it travels the same protected path as the rest of your traffic. Turn it off if you would rather your network saw nothing from Shroudly at all.
restartToApply: Changes apply right away; protection restarts for a moment.
routeListedDesc: Only the sites below go through Shroudly; everything else connects directly and uses your provider’s DNS. Choose this if you want the smallest possible footprint.
routeAllDesc: Every site goes through Shroudly and gets its encrypted DNS, so a blocked site works without you having to name it first. Connections that are not blocked are passed straight through untouched, so your speed stays the same.
siteListHint: One domain per line. Subdomains are included automatically (discord.com also covers cdn.discord.com).
siteListAuto: Updated automatically from OONI measurements: {count} sites, list of {date}. Sites blocked somewhere are added, and dropped again once they no longer are.
siteListCustom: This is your own list, so it is not updated automatically.
logSiteListUpdated: Site list updated: {count} sites ({added} added, {removed} removed)
logSiteListRefused: Site list: the downloaded list was refused ({detail})
logSiteListUnreachable: Site list: could not check for a newer list ({detail})
blockedNoticeTitle: {host} would not open with any method
blockedNoticeAdvanced: Your network blocks this more deeply than the normal mode can reach. Advanced mode works at the packet layer and usually gets through; it asks for administrator permission and undoes everything when you stop.
blockedNoticeNoAdvanced: Advanced mode is not available on this system, so there is nothing further to try automatically. The Logs tab has the detail — sending it to us is the fastest way to get this fixed.
restartAppsBody: A program reads the connection settings once, when it opens. {apps} was already running, so it is still using the unprotected connection it started with. Close it completely and open it again.
obBody1: When a site is blocked, your provider usually spots it by the site name in your very first packet, or by answering your DNS lookup with a lie. Shroudly reshapes that packet and looks names up over encrypted DNS, so the site loads normally. Your traffic still goes straight to the site — this is not a VPN and it does not hide who you are.
obBody2: Press Start and Shroudly points your system at itself while it runs. Press Stop and your network settings go back exactly as they were — and they are restored anyway if the app crashes, is force-quit, or the machine loses power. You never have to undo anything by hand.
obBody3: By default every site goes through Shroudly, and a site that is not blocked is passed on untouched — so nothing slows down and a blocked site works even if you have never heard of it. In Settings you can narrow this to a list of sites instead, and add or remove sites in that list whenever you like.
obTitle4: If a site still won’t open
obBody4: Open Settings and use the site test: it tries the site for real and tells you what is blocking it. The Logs tab records what happened for every site, which is exactly what we need if you report a problem. On Windows and Linux there is also Advanced mode for networks that the normal mode cannot get past.
obTitle5: If you need to ask us
obBody5: This tab records what Shroudly did: your system, your network, and for each site the technique that worked or how many were tried before giving up. If something does not work, copy what is here and send it with your report — it usually answers the question on its own, with no back and forth.
logSiteStillBlocked: {host}: still blocked after {tries} techniques ({family}) — this network may need Advanced mode
logConflict: Also running: {tools}. Another bypass tool or VPN changes the same connections as Shroudly; if sites misbehave, turn one of them off.
logDnsForgedFixed: Your DNS is being tampered with ({hosts}). Encrypted DNS has been switched back on automatically.
logDnsForgedHandled: Your provider returns forged DNS answers for {hosts}; Shroudly’s encrypted DNS is handling it.
logDohDown: Encrypted DNS is not reachable on this network; lookups are falling back to ordinary DNS, which your provider can read and change.
probeBlockedAdvancedOn: This test only checks the normal mode, so it cannot see what Advanced mode is doing. Advanced mode is on: open {host} or its app directly to check whether it now loads. If it is an app, close it completely and reopen it first.
logAppsNeedRestart: {apps} was already open when protection started — close it completely and reopen it so it uses the protected connection.
dnsAutoEnabledNotice: {host} could not be opened with encrypted DNS switched off, so it has been switched back on. Try the site again.
logDnsReenabledForBlock: {host} could not be opened with encrypted DNS switched off. It has been switched back on.
discordModeDesc: Lets the Discord app update and open through Shroudly. Adds one line to Discord's settings file; turning this off removes it.
discordOfferTitle: Is the Discord app stuck on “Checking for updates”?
discordOfferBody: Discord's updater skips Shroudly, so the filter still stops it. Shroudly can take it through itself by adding one line to Discord's settings file. The line is removed when you quit Shroudly or turn this off in Settings.
discordRestartNeeded: Restart Discord so its updates go through Shroudly.
discordPermission: Before the Discord app can use Shroudly, macOS has to allow Shroudly to change Discord's settings.
discordEditFailed: Discord's settings file could not be changed. To do it yourself, add this line to it: {line}
logDiscordOn: Discord app mode on: Discord updates through Shroudly
logDiscordOff: Discord app mode off: Discord settings restored
appModeDesc: Sends Roblox, its installer and other programs that ignore the system proxy through Shroudly as well. Programs that were already open need to be restarted.
appBrowserNote: Start Roblox with Open Roblox or from the Start menu: one started from a browser that was already open goes around Shroudly.
appOfferTitle: Does Roblox open in the browser but not as an app?
appOfferBody: The Roblox app and its installer ignore the system proxy, so the filter still stops them. Shroudly can take them through itself, along with other programs that do the same. Nothing is installed, and the setting is removed when you quit Shroudly or turn this off in Settings.
appRestartNeeded: Restart Roblox so it goes through Shroudly.
appForeign: A proxy for programs (HTTPS_PROXY) is already set on this computer, so Shroudly left it as it is. Games and apps mode can only work once it is removed.
appFailed: Games and apps mode could not be turned on. The log has the details.
logAppsOn: Games and apps mode on: Roblox and similar programs go through Shroudly
logAppsOff: Games and apps mode off: settings restored
logAppsForeign: Games and apps: another proxy is already set for programs (HTTPS_PROXY), so it was left as it is
logAppsLeftover: Games and apps: a setting left by an earlier run was removed
conflictBody: It reroutes the same connections as Shroudly, and the two get in each other's way. Quit {tools} completely while you use Shroudly.
cutTitle: {host} connects, then the network cuts it
cutBodyAdvanced: This network follows whole connections, not just how they start. Shroudly is already trying other techniques for this site; Advanced mode works below that level and usually gets through.
cutBodyAdvancedOn: Advanced mode is on and the network still cuts it. It is most likely blocking the server's address, which no technique can change; for this site only a VPN gets through.
cutBodyNoAdvanced: Shroudly is already trying other techniques for this site. If it keeps happening, the network is blocking the server's address or needs Advanced mode, which only Windows and Linux have; a VPN is then the remaining option.
dnsDownTitle: Encrypted DNS is blocked on this network
dnsDownBody: Shroudly keeps trying other routes on its own. Until one gets through, some sites may be sent to fake addresses; the fake addresses Shroudly knows are refused.
logCut: {host}: connects, then the network cuts it ({reason} after {kb} KB). Shroudly is trying other techniques for it.
logRegion: DNS answers on this network match the filtering used in {country}.
logDnsFilterService: Your DNS service filters sites; Shroudly's encrypted DNS goes around it.
logConflictGone: The other VPN or bypass tool is no longer running.
advancedRowDesc: For networks that follow whole connections, not just how they start — as in Iran, China or Russia. Use it when sites still load blank or keep stopping with protection on.
logIdleVpn: {tools} is installed but not connected; that does not interfere.
logPortMoved: Port {from} is in use by another program; Shroudly is using {to} instead.
ipv6Unavailable: Your network doesn’t support IPv6, so this option is unavailable.
testSiteDesc: Check which strategy unblocks a specific domain
testNeedsProtection: Start protection first, then run the test.
probeNotBlocked: {host} is not blocked on this network
probeDnsBlocked: {host} is blocked by DNS here, but DNS protection resolved it — it works
probeBlockedDesc: Split and disorder can't get past this DPI; it probably reassembles TCP streams (as in Iran or China). You can try Advanced mode, which uses packet-level fake-packet desync.
probeNoAnswer: No result yet. Check the Logs tab for details.
advancedAdminHint: Your system will ask for administrator permission.
advancedUnavailable: Advanced mode isn't available on this system.
advReasonMacUnsupported: Advanced mode isn't available on macOS: it would need a signed system network extension. The default engine still works.

advReasonNotBuilt: This build of Shroudly doesn't include the Advanced engine.
advReasonWindivertMissing: The WinDivert driver files are missing. Please reinstall Shroudly.
advReasonLinuxLibMissing: Install the libnetfilter-queue1 package first, for example: {command}
advReasonPlatformUnsupported: Advanced mode isn't supported on this operating system.
advErrorElevationUnavailable: Shroudly can't ask for administrator rights on this system (pkexec/polkit is missing). Run Shroudly as root instead.
advErrorStartFailed: The Advanced engine failed to start.
advErrorTimeout: The Advanced engine did not respond in time.
advErrorGeneric: Could not turn on Advanced mode.
logEngineGaveUp: Engine keeps crashing; giving up. Check the logs.
logRecovering: Recovering: restoring proxy settings from the previous session
logProbeBlocked: Auto: {host} stays blocked; split/disorder can't defeat this DPI
logProxyApplied: System traffic routed through the local proxy on port {port}
logProxyRecoveredPrevious: System proxy from the previous session restored
logProxyLegacyOff: System proxy left by an earlier version switched off
logProxyFailed: Could not set the system proxy: {detail}
logAdvancedAskingAdmin: Advanced mode: asking for administrator permission
logAdvancedNoStopConfirm: Advanced backend did not confirm the stop; it will exit when Shroudly quits
technique_frag_desc: The first TCP packet of each connection is split into small segments. DPI systems that don't reassemble TCP streams can't read the full Host/SNI field and let the connection through.
technique_disorder_desc: Segments are sent out of order (last one first). The destination's TCP stack puts them back together correctly, but DPI systems that read packets in sequence can't identify the connection.
technique_dns_desc: Names are resolved through several independent public resolvers at once and forged answers are discarded, so DNS-based blocking is defeated without changing your system DNS settings.
technique_http_desc: For plain HTTP connections the "Host:" header is rewritten as "hoSt:". Simple DPI systems that look for the exact text "Host:" no longer find it.
safetyDesc: By default Shroudly needs no driver and no administrator rights: while active it only points your system at a local proxy, and it restores the previous setting when it stops, crashes or you sign out, so your connection is never left broken. Advanced mode is optional and only runs if you turn it on.
technique_probe_desc: When a site stays blocked, Shroudly tests each bypass strategy against it over a real connection and remembers the one that works, so the next visit uses it right away.
technique_advanced_desc: Against DPI that reassembles connections (as in Iran or China), Shroudly can send a decoy copy of the first packet that the filter reads but that expires before it reaches the site. Available on Windows and Linux, it needs administrator permission and only runs when you turn it on.
updatesDesc: Shroudly checks GitHub for new versions when it starts and every 30 minutes.
updLaterHint: It will be installed the next time Shroudly quits.
updManual: Shroudly can’t update itself from this location. Move it to the Applications folder, or download the new version.
updError: Couldn’t check for updates. Shroudly will try again later.
updUnsupported: Automatic updates are not available in this build.
openSourceDesc: Shroudly is free and open source under the MIT license: anyone can read, audit and build its code.
autoUpdateDesc: Download new versions in the background and restart Shroudly to install them
appInstallStarted: Roblox's installer has started, through Shroudly.
appInstallFailed: Roblox could not be downloaded. Check that protection is on and try again; the details are in Logs.
appInstallUnsigned: The downloaded file was not signed by Roblox, so it was deleted and not started.
appBypassTitle: Roblox is not going through Shroudly
appBypassBody: It was probably started by a browser that was already open, so it connects directly and stays blocked. Restart it through Shroudly.
appStoreEdition: The Microsoft Store edition of Roblox cannot reach Shroudly. Install the regular edition with Install Roblox.
quitAppDesc: Stops protection and puts every setting back.
probeServiceBody: The network is no longer in the way: {host} answers, but turns the connection away (a block page, or silence after connecting). That is usually the site limiting access from your country. Shroudly never changes your address, so it cannot change this.
logAppsFirst: Games and apps: the first program connected through Shroudly ({host})
logAppsRoblox: Games and apps: Roblox is connecting through Shroudly
logAppsBypass: Games and apps: Roblox is running but none of its connections go through Shroudly (it was probably started by a browser that was already open)
logRobloxInstalled: Roblox installer downloaded through Shroudly and started ({version})
logRobloxUnsigned: The downloaded Roblox installer was not signed by Roblox, so it was deleted and not started
logUpdateWaiting: Update ready: it installs once Roblox and Discord are closed, or when Shroudly quits
logNoTray: No tray on this desktop: the window is minimised instead of closed
logServiceRefused: {host}: the site itself refuses this connection; Shroudly does not change your address, so it cannot change this
proxyAdminTitle: An administrator password is needed once
proxyAdminBody: This account may not change network settings, so browsers and most programs are not going through Shroudly yet. An administrator can allow it once; stopping protection needs no password.
proxyReplacedTitle: Another program changed the proxy settings
proxyReplacedBody: Browsers and most programs no longer go through Shroudly. Close the other proxy or VPN program, then set Shroudly again.
proxyEnvFirefoxNow: Firefox now goes through Shroudly. Chrome, Edge, Brave and other Chromium browsers will after you log out and back in.
proxyEnvRelogin: Chrome, Edge, Brave and other Chromium browsers will go through Shroudly after you log out and back in. For Firefox, enter {pac} as the automatic proxy configuration URL in its network settings.
proxyEnvChromiumNow: Chrome, Edge, Brave and other Chromium browsers go through Shroudly. For Firefox, enter {pac} as the automatic proxy configuration URL in its network settings.
proxyEnvFirefoxOnly: Firefox goes through Shroudly, but Chrome, Edge, Brave and other Chromium browsers could not be pointed at it on this desktop. The details are in Logs.
proxyNoneBody: This desktop has no system-wide proxy setting, so programs are not pointed at Shroudly automatically. In your browser, set the automatic proxy configuration address to {pac}.
proxyFailedBody: The system proxy could not be set, so browsers and most programs are not going through Shroudly. The details are in Logs.
logProxyRecoverPending: System proxy from the previous session could not be restored yet
logProxyOursAgain: The system proxy points at Shroudly again
logKdeLocked: KDE proxy settings are locked by the administrator
logProxyRestorePending: System proxy settings could not be restored yet; they will be at the next start
logProxyAdminNoChange: The system proxy did not change, although the administrator password was accepted
logProxyLegacyOffFailed: A system proxy left by an earlier version could not be switched off
logProxyEnvFirefoxNow: Firefox goes through Shroudly now; Chrome and other Chromium browsers will after you log out and back in
logProxyEnvRelogin: Chrome and other Chromium browsers will go through Shroudly after you log out and back in; Firefox has to be set by hand
logProxyEnvChromiumNow: Chrome and other Chromium browsers go through Shroudly; Firefox has to be set by hand
logProxyEnvFirefoxOnly: Firefox goes through Shroudly; Chrome and other Chromium browsers could not be set on this desktop
logProxyEnvRemoved: Browser settings for the next login removed
logProxyEnvPortMoved: The address browsers use to reach Shroudly had to change; Chrome and other Chromium browsers follow the new one after you log out and back in
logUnreachableDns: {host}: could not be reached (its name could not be looked up)
logUnreachableConnect: {host}: could not be reached (no connection to its server)
logSiteNoAnswer: {host}: no answer after {tries} techniques ({family}) — the network may be dropping these connections silently, or the site is down
logProxyReplaced: Another program changed the system proxy ({what}): that traffic no longer goes through Shroudly
logLocalDns: System DNS is a program on this computer: {programs}
logDnsDead: The system DNS answered none of the test names. Programs that do not go through Shroudly cannot reach anything; check the DNS program or the network settings.
trayMinimized: Shroudly keeps running in the tray
notifyUpdateReady: Version {version} is ready. Shroudly will restart to install it.
notifySiteBlockedBody: {host} would not open with any method. Advanced mode may get through on this network.
notifyAppBypassTitle: Roblox is not going through Shroudly
notifyAppBypassBody: It was probably started by a browser that was already open, so it stays blocked. Open Shroudly to restart it through Shroudly.
discordPickMessage: macOS needs your permission to change Discord's settings. Discord's folder is already open: just click “Allow access”.
proxyAdminPrompt: Shroudly needs an administrator's password to point this Mac's network proxy settings at it. Stopping protection will not ask again.
proxyAdminPromptRestore: Shroudly needs an administrator's password to put this Mac's network proxy settings back.
proxyRecoverTitle: This Mac's proxy settings still point at Shroudly
proxyRecoverBody: Shroudly could not put them back after the Mac restarted, because that needs an administrator's password. Some programs may not connect until they are back.
proxyEnvNotTakenFirefox: Firefox goes through Shroudly. This session does not read the setting Shroudly writes for Chrome, Edge, Brave and other Chromium browsers at login, so they do not: start them with --proxy-pac-url={pac}, or set auto_proxy={pac} where your session sets its variables.
proxyEnvNotTaken: This session does not read the setting Shroudly writes for Chrome, Edge, Brave and other Chromium browsers at login: start them with --proxy-pac-url={pac}, or set auto_proxy={pac} where your session sets its variables. For Firefox, enter {pac} as the automatic proxy configuration URL in its network settings.
proxyEnvChromiumRestart: Chrome, Brave, VS Code and other Chromium-based apps that were already open before Shroudly started may connect directly until you close and reopen them.

logProxyRestoreDeclined: Administrator password not given; the proxy settings were not put back

logGsettingsFailed: Could not change GNOME's proxy setting: {detail}
